data.title: Susceptibility to QR Code Phishing
data.summary: Staff scanned QR codes from unsolicited messages and from printed notices placed on the premises, and authenticated on the pages they led to. The code moves the attack to a personal phone, outside mail filtering and device controls.
data.description:
A QR code is an unreadable link. The protections built around links — hover preview, reputation filtering, rewriting in mail gateways — do not apply, because the destination is not visible and the mail body may contain no URL at all.

Scanning usually moves the victim to a personal phone, which is outside device management and often outside the organisation's controls entirely, and where a small screen makes the address bar easy to ignore.

The physical variant is stronger still: a printed notice placed in a lobby or a car park carries the authority of being physically present in the building.
data.recommendation:
* Tell staff that a QR code is a link they cannot read, and that codes arriving by message or found on site should be treated as untrusted.
* Deploy phishing-resistant MFA, which makes the credential harvested this way useless.
* Scan mail attachments for embedded codes where the gateway supports it.
* Include QR pretexts, printed as well as emailed, in simulations.
data.short_recommendation: Treat QR codes as untrusted links; verify before scanning.
